# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This is the online version of **Transitioning from R Markdown
to Quarto: A One-Week Boot Camp** by The rgtlab Curriculum
Project. We wrote it for analysts who already write R
Markdown and wish to move their work to Quarto.

We cover what an experienced R Markdown user needs in order
to become fluent in Quarto over one week. That is,
installing Quarto and rendering an existing `.Rmd` file
unchanged; the document anatomy that differs from R
Markdown, including the `#|` cell-option syntax and the
execution model; output formats, figures, tables, and native
cross-references; projects at scale, from websites to books
to manuscripts; and reproducible publishing, with a
systematic checklist for migrating a real project. The book
is designed for **five consecutive days** of work: one hour
of lecture content each day, two hours of homework, no
examinations.

Our organizing principle is that Quarto is a superset of
what R Markdown already does. The transition is therefore a
matter of translation and extension rather than of starting
over. An analyst who can write an `.Rmd` file today already
knows most of what Quarto asks. We map the familiar
constructs onto their Quarto equivalents and then show what
Quarto adds beyond them. Each chapter opens with a concrete
authoring problem, develops the Quarto mechanism that
addresses it, and returns to the problem to judge what the
mechanism did and did not solve.

The workshop is a companion to the rgtlab curriculum
sequence:

- **R for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp**
  (<https://r-bootcamp.rgtlab.org>), the preparatory volume
  for R.
- [*Git and GitHub for Biostatistics*](https://git-bootcamp.rgtlab.org),
  the preparatory volume for version control, on which the
  publishing chapter of this workshop draws.
- [*Biostatistics Practicum*](https://rgtlab.org/practicum),
  workflow infrastructure (Git in depth, Docker, renv,
  Quarto, CDISC) that builds directly on this workshop.
- [*Reproducible Research for the Health Sciences*](https://reproducibility.rgtlab.org),
  the reproducibility volume that extends the freeze,
  caching, and publishing material introduced here.

A reader who has completed *R for Biostatistics* and *Git and
GitHub for Biostatistics* arrives at this workshop ready to
place a Quarto project under version control and publish it
reproducibly by the end of the week.

We refer the reader to the [Preface](preface.qmd) for the
design rationale and to the [Conventions](conventions.qmd)
page for the visual cues used throughout.
